'''''Platanthera azorica''''', commonly known as '''Hochstetter's butterfly orchid''', is a species of [[orchid]] in the genus ''[[Platanthera]]''. It was "rediscovered" in 2011 on a single [[volcano|volcanic]] [[ridge]] on the central [[Azores]] island of [[São Jorge Island|São Jorge]], and "is arguably Europe's rarest ''bona fide'' orchid species."<ref name=BatemanRudall2013>{{cite journal|last1=Bateman|first1=Richard M.|last2=Rudall|first2=Paula J.|last3=Moura|first3=Mónica|title=Systematic revision of ''Platanthera'' in the Azorean archipelago: not one but three species, including arguably Europe's rarest orchid|journal=PeerJ|volume=1|year=2013|article-number=e218|issn=2167-8359|doi=10.7717/peerj.218|pmid=24392284|pmc=3869205 |doi-access=free }}</ref> While ''P. azorica'' was previously considered by some sources to be the same as ''[[Platanthera micrantha]]'',<ref name=iucn2011 /> the 2011 discovery triggered a thorough analysis of historic and current data and specimens, resulting in three species identified.

== Distribution ==
At the time of its rediscovery, the species was only known to grow in a single small upland area of São Jorge.<ref name=BatemanRudall2013 /> The same island was not included in Hochstetter's expedition, meaning that the specimen that was originally collected in 1838 was from another island.<ref name=ScienceDaily2013 /> A 2017 discovery of a flowering specimen in the neighboring island of [[Faial Island|Faial]] reaffirmed its presence in other islands of the archipelago.<ref>{{cite web |title=Platanthera azorica Schltr. |url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/1platanthera+azorica |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=29 December 2021}}</ref>

== Origin ==
[[Genetic testing]] confirms that the lineage of the species derives from Europe or North Africa, rather than North America as had been previously hypothesized, and evidence suggests "that the Azorean lineage represents a single migration of seed to the archipelago from a mainland European population [...]"<ref name= BatemanRudall2013 />

== Description ==
There are now three distinct species of Azorean butterfly orchids:
* '''''P. azorica''''' Schlt.: The exceptionally rare rediscovered species is now correctly identified as ''P. azorica'', commonly named '''Hochstetter's butterfly orchid''' in honor of German botanist Karl Hochstetter.<ref name=BatemanRudall2013 /> Hochstetter originally found a specimen in 1838 during a scientific expedition to six of the nine Azores islands, which was not distinguished from the other species.<ref name=Khan2013>{{cite news | last=Khan | first=Amina | title=Rare butterfly orchid discovered on volcanic island ridge in Azores | work=Los Angeles Times | date=10 December 2013 | url=http://www.latimes.com/science/sciencenow/la-sci-sn-rare-butterfly-orchid-volcanic-ridge-azores-island-20131210,0,3876980.story?track=rss | access-date=11 December 2013 }}</ref> The flower is "exceptionally large" compared to the other two species.<ref name=ScienceDaily2013>{{cite web | work=ScienceDaily | title=Europe's Rarest Orchid Rediscovered On 'Lost World' Volcano in the Azores | date=10 December 2013 | url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/12/131210072117.htm | access-date=11 December 2013 }}</ref>
* '''''[[Platanthera micrantha|P. micrantha]]''''' (Hochst.) Schltr.: The misidentified species previously known as ''P. azorica'' is now correctly named ''P. micrantha'', commonly named the '''narrow-lipped butterfly orchid'''. Found on eight of the nine islands, it is much more rare than ''P. pollostantha'', occurring in smaller, scattered populations.<ref name=BatemanRudall2013 />
* '''''P. pollostantha''''': The misidentified species previously known as ''P. micrantha'' is now redescribed as ''P. pollostantha'', sp. nov., commonly named the '''short-spurred butterfly orchid'''. This is the most common of the three species, and is found on all nine islands of the Azores.<ref name=BatemanRudall2013 />

== Conservation status ==

The previously known ''P. micrantha'' was listed by the [[IUCN Red List|IUCN Red List of Threatened Species]] as Vulnerable,<ref name=iucn2011>{{cite iucn |author=Rankou, H. |date=2011 |title=''Platanthera micrantha'' |volume=2011 |article-number=e.T175973A7159797 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2011-2.RLTS.T175973A7159797.en |access-date=11 November 2021}}</ref> but that was under the assumption that all three Azorean butterfly orchids comprised a single species. Justification was given that the population is decreasing due to threats such as destruction of the habitat to create pastures, invasive plants and road construction.<ref name=iucn2011 />

The 2013 study that described the three distinct species stated that the prior Red List [[threat assessment]] be overturned because the species is Europe's rarest ''bona fide'' orchid species, and ''P. micrantha'', an equally rare species, is a good indicator for the amount of semi-natural [[laurisilva]] habitats remaining on the Azores.<ref name=BatemanRudall2013 />
